Learner adapters for shared_importance()

Source: R/learners.R
sharedimp_learner.Rd

A learner is a pair of functions, fit(x, y) and predict(model, x), where x is a numeric matrix with column names (a representation built by build_representations()). For regression, predict() must return a numeric vector with one value per row of x. For classification it must return a numeric matrix of class probabilities with one column per level of y, in level order (column names are optional). Predicted class labels are always derived by shared_importance() as the argmax of that matrix.

Usage

sharedimp_learner(fit, predict, label = "custom learner")

Arguments

fit

A function function(x, y) returning a fitted model object.

predict

A function function(model, x) returning predictions in the format described above.

label

A short description used in printing.

Value

An object of class sharedimp_learner.

Details

shared_importance() accepts three kinds of learner:

  • a string: "rand_forest" (default; ranger with 500 trees and min_n = 5, mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(x)))) or "linear" (ordinary least squares via stats::lm.fit(), unpenalized logistic regression via stats::glm.fit(), or multinomial logistic regression via nnet::multinom(), depending on the task; aliased coefficients are set to zero);

  • a parsnip model specification whose mode matches the task, used as is (its hyperparameters are fixed; nothing is tuned);

  • an object created by sharedimp_learner().

Examples

ols <- sharedimp_learner(
  fit = function(x, y) stats::lm.fit(cbind(1, x), y),
  predict = function(model, x) {
    beta <- model$coefficients
    beta[is.na(beta)] <- 0
    drop(cbind(1, x) %*% beta)
  },
  label = "OLS via lm.fit"
)
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(200), 50, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("x", 1:4)))
y <- x[, 1] + rnorm(50)
shared_importance(x, y, learner = ols, v = 3, seed = 1)
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       regression
#>   learner:    OLS via lm.fit
#>   metric:     mse (minimize); score = -mse, importance = score_full - score_reduced
#>   resampling: 3-fold cross-validation (1 repeat)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   feature importance importance_std score_full score_reduced n_splits
#>   <chr>        <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 x1          0.365          0.874       -1.70         -2.07        3
#> 2 x2         -0.0707         0.0569      -1.70         -1.63        3
#> 3 x3          0.0961         0.0603      -1.70         -1.80        3
#> 4 x4         -0.189          0.455       -1.70         -1.51        3
